samples.summary: Read-only context menu still cannot offer Copy for a click-selected image; with only an image selected the menu does not open at all
samples.evidence: `hasSelection` comes from `editor.getActiveSelection()` (editor.ts:3311), which returns null unless there is a non-collapsed *text* range — it knows nothing about `selectedImage`. So in read-only with only an image selected: `hasSpellGroup=false` (spell is skipped when readOnly), `hasClipboardGroup = !readOnly || hasSelection = false`, `hasInsertGroup=false` → line 84 bails and no menu opens; at render time `showCopy = hasSelection` (line 181) would hide Copy anyway. This directly contradicts the justification written into the change (editor.ts:1251-1252: "the issue #870 fix never runs on a read-only document — which is exactly where the context menu now offers Copy"). The keyboard shortcut path still works, so the reach is limited to the menu affordance.

samples.summary: `selectImageAt` / `getSelectedImage` / `updateSelectedImage` still use the throwing `doc.getBlock()` behind a dead `if (!block) return` guard
samples.evidence: `selectImageAt` (line 3771, body rewritten by this diff) does `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId); if (!block) return;` — `Doc.getBlock` throws `Error(\`Block not found\`)` (model/document.ts:187) rather than returning undefined, so the null check can never fire and an unknown/stale blockId throws out of the API instead of no-oping. `getSelectedImage` (3780) and `updateSelectedImage` (3793) have the same pattern and read the same `selectedImage` coordinate that the diff now explicitly acknowledges can go stale after a remote edit — this is exactly the hazard the new `imageSelectionProvider` (2320) was changed to avoid by using `findBlock`. The sibling readers were left unconverted. No production caller of `getSelectedImage` exists today (grep found none outside tests), which caps the impact.
searchedFor: grep getSelectedImage across packages (frontend: no matches)

samples.summary: Table-structure mutators (deleteTable / deleteTableRow / deleteTableColumn / insertTableRow / insertTableColumn) never call `clearImageSelectionForMutation`, contradicting its "every entry point" doc comment
samples.evidence: The comment at editor.ts:1267-1274 claims every mutating entry point routes through `clearImageSelectionForMutation` first, and the diff adds calls in insertLink/insertTable/insertImage/insertPageNumber/applySpellSuggestion. But `deleteTable` (3580), `deleteTableRow` (3623), `deleteTableColumn` (3648), `insertTableRow` (3614) and `insertTableColumn` (3639) mutate structure — including removing the very block a selected image lives in — without clearing. The result is a `selectedImage` naming a deleted block; the overlay silently vanishes, and any `getSelectedImage()` call in that state throws (see the related getBlock finding).
searchedFor: grep '^    (insert|delete|apply|replace|set)[A-Za-z]*: ' over editor.ts to enumerate mutating EditorAPI members

samples.summary: In read-only, clicking a hyperlinked image both selects it and opens the link in a new tab, so the newly-enabled viewer image copy is unreachable for linked images
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` now runs in read-only and calls `textEditorRef?.recordReadOnlyLinkAtMouse(e)` (2614) before `selectImageInline` (2618), which does `selection.setRange(null)`. `TextEditor.handleMouseUp` (text-editor.ts:2005-2015) then sees `readOnlyPendingLinkHref` set and a collapsed/null range and calls `window.open(href)`. So for a hyperlinked image a viewer's click always navigates away in a new tab; the image selection the copy path depends on is established but the user is taken to another tab first, and there is no click that selects such an image without navigating.
searchedFor: read handleImageMouseDown hit branch in editor.ts

samples.summary: Read-only image clicks now swallow the mousedown, so a viewer can no longer begin a text drag-selection on an image (and open UI listening on document mousedown never sees the event)
samples.evidence: `handleImageMouseDown` previously returned immediately when `readOnly` (removed line `if (readOnly) return;`). It now calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` on any image hit (2615-2616), so `TextEditor.handleMouseDown` never runs for that press: `isMouseDown` is never set and no drag selection can start from an image, and document-level bubble listeners (e.g. the docs context menu's outside-click closer, docs-context-menu.tsx:126) never receive the mousedown. Previously read-only image clicks fell through to both.
searchedFor: grep addEventListener('mousedown' across docs/src and frontend docs components

samples.summary: `clearImageSelectionForMutation` triggers a full `render()` immediately before the mutation that will render again
samples.evidence: Every new call site (insertLink 3197, insertTable 3534, insertImage 3749, insertPageNumber 3831, applySpellSuggestion 3443, and TextEditor.applyPastePlan 1353 / handleCut 1260) invokes it before the write, and the function calls the editor's full `render()` (1285) when an image was selected; the mutation path then renders again. Correctness is unaffected — it is a wasted layout pass, and in the paste case it happens inside the paste's synchronous window.
searchedFor: read clearImageSelectionForMutation and its call sites

finding.evidence:
The change establishes the rule that "[e]very entry point that mutates text while an image selection can still be live routes through here first" (editor.ts:1264-1274) and wires cut/paste/applySpellSuggestion/insertTable/insertImage/insertPageNumber. Two production mutation paths are not wired and are not preceded by a canvas keydown that would hit the catch-all:
1. `applyLink` — `doc.insertText(pos, url)` at editor.ts:3217. Reached from the toolbar link button / link popover (`docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:606,674` → `requestLink` → popover → `editor.applyLink(url)`); the popover input holds focus, so no keydown reaches `imageKeyHandler`. Inserting text shifts every offset after `pos`, leaving `selectedImage` naming a different inline.
2. `FindReplaceState.replaceActive` / `replaceAll` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:57,69,78) mutate `doc` directly from `docs-find-bar.tsx:118,126` — a React button click, again no editor keydown. `replaceMatch` deletes then inserts, so a replacement shorter than the match slides a *later* inline (possibly another image) onto the selected offset.
The new re-validation in `deleteSelectedImageInline` / `imageSelectionProvider` only checks that *an* image sits at the offset, so a second image sliding into that slot is copied/cut/deleted instead of the one the user selected.

verdict.reason: Both claimed bypasses are not present as described. (1) There is no `applyLink` anywhere in the repo; the toolbar/popover link path is `editor.insertLink(url)` (docs-link-popover.tsx:139), and `insertLink` (editor.ts:3192) calls `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` at editor.ts:3197 before all branches, including the caret branch's `doc.insertText(pos, url)` at editor.ts:3253 — with a comment at 3193-3196 citing exactly the "toolbar-driven, no keydown" scenario. (2) The find bar already clears: `editor?.clearImageSelection()` at docs-find-bar.tsx:124 precedes `state.replaceActive(...)` (125) and at :133 precedes `state.replaceAll(...)` (134), with the offset-shift rationale documented at 115-120; `clearImageSelection` is the exported alias of the same helper (editor.ts:3777, interface editor.ts:319), and the helper's docstring (editor.ts:1276-1281) plus copy-integrity.test.ts:1084-1094 cover this out-of-module path. The only other `doc.insertText(pos, url)` is text-box-editor.ts:1217, an editor with no image-selection state at all (no `selectedImage`/`imageSelection` occurrences in that file), so it cannot bypass the rule.
